builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
summary: LoopZip replaces full-length visual token sequences in looped (weight-shared) VLMs with a compressed set built from pre-backbone aggregation, cross-invocation attention-based token selection, and weight-tied value correction, all without additional training. It costs implementation complexity in the inference path and a small quality loss (about 2.8% at 50% pruning, degrading further at higher ratios), while saving roughly 58% peak GPU memory and about 2x latency. It can fail if the reader's production model is not a looped VLM, since the cross-invocation selection and value correction mechanisms assume shared layers called multiple times, and gains may not transfer to standard VLMs or workloads with few visual tokens.
rationale: The method is training-free and runs on a single consumer GPU, but it applies only to looped weight-shared VLMs, so the reader must verify their deployed architecture matches before adopting it.
technique: Training-free visual token compression for looped VLMs

claims.statement: LoopZip replaces full-length visual token sequences in looped (weight-shared) VLMs with a compressed set built from pre-backbone aggregation, cross-invocation attention-based token selection, and weight-tied value correction, all without additional training. It costs implementation complexity in the inference path and a small quality loss (about 2.8% at 50% pruning, degrading further at higher ratios), while saving roughly 58% peak GPU memory and about 2x latency. It can fail if the reader's production model is not a looped VLM, since the cross-invocation selection and value correction mechanisms assume shared layers called multiple times, and gains may not transfer to standard VLMs or workloads with few visual tokens.

On LoopVL-1B, LoopZip retains 97.16% of original performance at 50% token pruning and, across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang, reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 58.36%-58.98% with 2.01-2.47x end-to-end speedups over the unpruned model.
